transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time letting go of certain thoughts. I know that sounds vague, sorry. It’s like I keep thinking I’ve missed something important—like a wrong number in a data release, or that I left the back door unlocked, or paid a bill from the wrong account. Even when I’m pretty sure I checked, my mind keeps going back to it like maybe I caused some big problem. I know that probably sounds a bit excessive, but it’s been… difficult.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, counting, or going through specific mental rituals—to try to ease the worry or make sure everything is ‘just right’?

Yes… I do, though I try not to let it get out of hand. I’ll reopen spreadsheets and go back through emails line by line, just to make sure I didn’t miss anything. And at home I check the locks, or payment confirmations, usually in the same order, because if I don’t it doesn’t feel… safe, I guess.

I know that probably sounds like a lot. Some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, checking, and somehow nothing is actually finished. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your work, relationships, or daily life?

I mean… yes, it does interfere, more than I’d like to admit. I try to tell myself I’m just being thorough, especially with my work, but I’ve fallen behind on some major deadlines because I stay late reviewing things and then still don’t actually finish.

And outside of work… I’ve stopped going to salsa nights, and I haven’t been kayaking much, because I can’t get away from the checking and reviewing in time. It sounds a little silly when I say it out loud, but it’s been affecting my life, yes.

When you’re going through your checks—like reviewing emails or spreadsheets—do you feel that you have to do it a certain way to prevent something bad from happening, or is it more that you just worry something might go wrong and want to be sure?

I think… it’s a bit of both, honestly. I tell myself I’m just trying to be certain, you know, being careful. But it does start to feel like I have to do it a certain way.

Like with spreadsheets, I’ll reopen them and check the numbers again, and then reread emails line by line. At home it’s locks or payment confirmations, and I tend to do it in the same order until it feels… safe, I guess. I know that may sound excessive. Some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and somehow I still haven’t really finished anything.

When you go through these checking rituals, is it mainly to reduce the anxiety or discomfort you feel about the possibility of something being wrong, or do you feel that something bad will actually happen if you don't do them?

I think it’s mostly to calm myself down, if I’m being honest. I don’t always think, like, “this exact bad thing will happen,” but the discomfort gets so strong that I feel like I can’t leave it alone.

So I’ll reopen the spreadsheet, reread the email line by line, check the locks or payment confirmation again… usually in the same order, until it feels safe enough. I know that probably sounds excessive. Some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and nothing is really finished, but in the moment it feels like the only way to settle myself.

Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that feel foreign to you—like fears of making a mistake that you can’t control—even if you know they’re unlikely, and do these thoughts cause you a lot of anxiety?

Yes… I think that’s actually the main thing. I get these thoughts that I’ve missed something critical, and I don’t want them there. Like a wrong number in a data release, or that I left the back door unlocked, or paid a bill from the wrong account.

Even when I know I checked it, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I could have caused some kind of disaster. I know it’s probably unlikely, and I feel a little embarrassed saying it like that, but yes, it makes me really anxious.
Do these rituals or checks you perform help reduce the anxiety or discomfort you feel, even if it’s only temporary?

Yes… it does help, at least for a little while. I mean, that’s why I keep doing it, I suppose.

If I reopen the spreadsheet, or reread the email carefully line by line, or check the lock or the payment confirmation again, I feel this sort of drop in tension. Not completely gone, but enough that I can breathe for a moment. I usually do it in the same order until it feels… safe, I guess.

I know that probably sounds like too much. And the relief doesn’t really last, because sometimes I’m still there hours later, especially at my desk, and I haven’t actually finished anything. But in the moment it feels like the only way to calm myself down.
When you perform these checks or rituals, is it mainly to prevent something bad from happening, or do you feel a need to do them to just feel right or complete?

I think it’s more the “feel right” part… or feel safe, maybe. I mean, I tell myself I’m preventing a mistake, but a lot of the time it’s that I just can’t settle unless I do it.

So I’ll reopen the spreadsheet, reread an email line by line, check the lock or the payment confirmation again, usually in the same order. And I know that sounds a bit much, but if I don’t do it, it feels unfinished somehow. Like I can’t move on.

Sometimes it takes much longer than I want to admit… there are nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and I haven’t really finished anything. But I keep thinking, “just one more check,” until it feels safe enough.

Are these worries about mistakes or disasters something you’ve always been more sensitive to, or do they feel different from your usual thoughts—like they come out of nowhere and are more intense than regular concerns?

They feel different from just my normal worrying, I think. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with my work and bills and the house, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming everything on this.

But these thoughts… they sort of hit me and won’t leave. Like, “What if there’s a wrong number in the data release?” or “What if the back door is unlocked?” or “What if I paid that bill from the wrong account?” And even if I know I already checked, my mind keeps going back to the possibility that I missed something critical and caused some kind of disaster.

I know that probably sounds dramatic. It’s just much more intense than a regular concern, and it feels very unwanted.
Do you ever have intrusive thoughts or feel the need to clean, organize, or arrange things in a specific way to reduce discomfort or anxiety?

I don’t think it’s really about cleaning, no… not especially. Organizing maybe a little, but more with checking things in a certain order, if that counts.

Like, to calm myself down, I’ll reopen spreadsheets, reread emails line by line, check the locks or payment confirmations again… and I tend to do it in the same sequence until it feels safe enough. I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything, it’s just hard to stop once that feeling is there.

Some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and I haven’t actually finished anything because I keep going back over it. It’s embarrassing to say, but that’s more what happens than cleaning or arranging things.

Do the thoughts you described—like worrying about a wrong number in a data release or leaving the door unlocked—feel like they’re coming from you, or do they feel more like they’re invading your mind and not what you want to be thinking?

They feel like they’re coming from my own mind, I guess… not like someone else is putting them there. But they don’t feel like thoughts I want to have.

It’s more like they barge in and then I can’t get them to leave. I’ll know I checked the number, or the door, or the bill payment, but then this awful thought keeps coming back—what if I missed something critical and caused a disaster? And I know that sounds a little extreme, I’m sorry, but it feels very hard to shake once it starts.

Have you ever had upsetting or disturbing thoughts that you wish you could get out of your mind—like thoughts of harming someone, or having inappropriate sexual thoughts, even if you would never act on them?

Not really the harming-someone or sexual kind, no… at least not that I can think of. I hope that’s okay to say.

For me it’s more these awful thoughts that I’ve missed something important—like a wrong number in a data release, or the back door being unlocked, or paying a bill from the wrong account. Even when I know I checked, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I caused some big disaster. It feels very unwanted, and I wish I could just push it out of my head.

When you perform your checking rituals, like reviewing emails or checking locks, do you feel that you must do them in a precise way or order to feel that things are 'just right,' even beyond just calming your anxiety?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I tell myself it’s just to calm down or be responsible, but it does have to be in a certain order or it doesn’t feel settled.

Like I’ll reopen the spreadsheet, then reread the email line by line, then check the confirmation or the lock again, and if I skip something or do it “wrong,” I feel like I have to go back and start over until it feels safe enough. Not perfect exactly… more like I can’t move on until it feels okay.

And I know that sounds excessive. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, and I haven’t really finished anything because I keep looping back through the same checks.
